title: The Typewriter of the Palatinate
premise: In 1911, on a windswept stretch of the Palatinate coast, widowed lighthouse keeper Oscar Reyes has spent five years perfecting invisibility after his wife's death made him a target of the town's suspicion. When the army requisitions the town during the year of the great storms, seizing the parish ledger that holds every family's name, Oscar realizes the document is being rewritten to erase a drowned fishing village's claim to the land. Using his late wife's typewriter and his position as the keeper of the only light still burning, he secretly records testimonies from the displaced families and smuggles the true record to a journalist in the capital before the victors' historians can seal the official version. He loses the lighthouse, nearly loses his life in the final storm, and loses his anonymity entirely—but in choosing to be seen, he finally finds where he belongs, among the people he once kept at arm's length.
about_author: Coral Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated municipal records from coastal Europe, where she first encountered ledgers with pages razored out. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people who refuse to let documents lie.

chapters.title: The Light That Answers No One
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Establishes his ritualized invisibility: he keeps the lighthouse, logs the weather, and speaks to no one beyond necessity, still grieving his wife Marta. When a fishing boat founders in the first great storm and he saves a boy, Ilan, the town notices him for the first time in five years. Emotional beat: the terror of being seen.

chapters.title: Requisition Papers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Army officers arrive, commandeer the harbor, and seize the parish ledger containing every family's name and land claim. The captain, Voss, is polite and absolute; the town's records will be 'held for review.' Oscar recognizes the clerk rewriting entries and remembers Marta's typewriter gathering dust upstairs. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Marta Left Behind
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with flashback to Marta's death and the accusations that followed. He oils the old typewriter and types a single test line, hearing her voice in the keys. Ilan returns to thank him and becomes an unwilling messenger between the lighthouse and the displaced families. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Drowned Parish
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Rosa, a matriarch of the flooded fishing village whose land claim the army is erasing. She begins dictating testimony to Oscar at night, one family at a time, while storms keep the soldiers off the water. Emotional beat: fragile trust forming between the keeper and the people who once shunned him.

chapters.title: Ledger and Lie
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He risks a visit to the requisitioned records office and confirms the original pages are being replaced; Voss's historians are building a case that the village never legally existed. A near-discovery forces him to hide the testimonies inside the lighthouse's lamp room. Emotional beat: the stakes become mortal.

chapters.title: The Storm Between Us
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. A soldier raids the village camp looking for 'the scribe,' and Rosa covers for Ilan, nearly paying with her freedom. She confronts Oscar: his silence kept him safe for five years, but their safety now depends on his voice. Emotional beat: love against duty—she asks him to choose.

chapters.title: Blackout
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Voss orders the lighthouse dark to strand a supply convoy's witnesses, and Oscar must choose between his orders, his light, and the truth. He keeps the lamp burning, openly defying the army for the first time, and is arrested. Emotional beat: the end of invisibility, embraced.

chapters.title: The Cell and the Key
chapters.summary: Rosa's POV. With Oscar imprisoned, Ilan smuggles the hidden testimonies out of the lamp room, and Rosa organizes the families to move the record to the coast road where a journalist's carriage is due. The greatest storm of the year breaks. Emotional beat: courage passed hand to hand.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, escaping during the storm's chaos as the sea floods the prison block. He races the rising water to the coast road, carrying the final pages—his own testimony about Marta—while the lighthouse beam, relit by Ilan, guides him through the dark. Emotional beat: the climax, where the record and the man both nearly drown.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, months later. The journalist's account forces an inquiry; the village's claim is restored, though Voss escapes punishment and the lighthouse is decommissioned. Oscar, no longer keeper, stays in town as its unofficial archivist, Rosa at his side. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—he has traded safety for belonging, and calls it a fair price.
